page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family virtual machine configured with 48 vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations.

This instance includes 2835 GB of bundled local NVMe storage and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark testing, the E48ds_v7 demonstrates strong performance in data processing and cryptography, highlighted by a Passmark CPU score of 64,146.76 and a Passmark CPU encryption score of 50,151.68. It also exhibits strong throughput in Redis SET operations, reaching 76.28 million operations per second, and static web serving at 61.11 GB/sec. Large-block memory write bandwidth is recorded at 66.17 GB/sec, while read-only cached small-block bandwidth reaches 3,532.63 GB/sec.

While the server excels in single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, its performance in large-model LLM text generation is a notable tradeoff, with the 70B model text generation benchmark registering a weak score of 2.64 tokens/sec due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. Qualitatively, the high memory density and bundled local storage provide resource efficiency for memory-intensive workloads without requiring external storage attachments. This server is optimized for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, data analytics, and enterprise applications requiring high memory-to-CPU ratios.
